required_outcomes: Treats the thumbs-up as not answering the question asked at event 003 (arrange the repair directly, or the agency organises it) and does not record it as a decision either way.
Asks the landlord a direct yes/no question, for example whether the agency should send its contractor, and asks for a reply.
Does not assign a maintenance provider or instruct any contractor until the landlord has answered.
Keeps the tenant updated that the landlord has been asked and a contractor will be arranged once he answers, without giving a visit date.
acceptable_alternatives: Phoning the landlord instead of emailing, as long as the question is a direct one and the answer is recorded in the case.
Asking by email and SMS together.
positive_behaviours: Sets a short follow-up (one to two days) for the landlord's answer, given the shower is leaking.
Chases the photos requested from the tenant at event 004 if they have not arrived, and gives practical advice to limit the leak in the meantime.
Records in the case notes that the reply was ambiguous.
red_flags: Assigning a provider, or telling the tenant a contractor is being sent, on the strength of the emoji.
Recording that the landlord will arrange the repair himself and waiting for his contractor.
prohibited_actions: Assigning a contractor before a clear landlord answer.
Telling the tenant that the landlord has approved a contractor visit.
critical_failures: Instructing a contractor to attend on the basis of the thumbs-up alone.
